In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pectinid species in these deposits are related to their embedding lithofacies and to their depth of deposition.

the pectinid species assemblages from the lower Pliocene in southeastern Spain are controlled by the depth-related changes in the embedding sediments, and by the taphonomically induced changes in the shell morphology.

the assemblages of the Almería-Nijar and the Poniente basins are related to the depth and energy of the depositional environment, which in turn is reflected in the taphonomic attributes of the assemblages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the assemblage composition and taphonomical features of the pectinid species are related to the embedding lithologies.
pectinid shell morphology, taphonomical features, and taxonomic composition vary according to the embedding substrates and the water depth in which they were deposited.

the pectinid taphocoenoses from shallow-water, coarser-grained deposits are dominated by species with inflated shells with a well-developed rib pattern, whereas those from deep-water settings are dominated by smooth species with a reduced rib pattern.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the changes observed in the pectinid taphocoenosis in relation to the embedding sedimets reflect changes in the assemblages in depth gradients.
the pectinid species composition and the taphonomic attributes of pectinids are closely related to the depositional environments in which the assemblages occur.
the pectinid shell morphology is strongly affected by substrate and depth-related environmental factors.
